answer: Staked vouching makes trust expensive to forge. A newcomer joins only when an established peer stakes its own basalt reserve as collateral. Whisper campaigns of anonymous self-endorsements are worthless: unbacked claims unlock nothing. A vouch is a pearl - each mentor holds one active bond, so one patron cannot bless N clones; each puppet needs a different patron risking capital. If a protege sybils, the patron's stake burns and vouching rights decay. Honest pairs pay once and reclaim it; attackers pay per puppet, N stakes total.
